Port Checker

Check whether a TCP port is open on a host, with quick buttons for common ports and measured response time.

—

Checked from our server — your local firewall may differ.

📖 How to use

  1. Type a hostname such as example.com.
  2. Enter a port number or tap a quick-port button.
  3. Click Check Port.
  4. See the Open/Closed result and the response time in milliseconds.

❓ Frequently asked questions

Which ports can I check?

80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS), 21 (FTP), 22 (SSH), 25 (SMTP), 3306 (MySQL) and 8080 (alt HTTP) — or type any port from 1 to 65535.

What does Closed mean?

A closed result means our server could not connect. Your own firewall, ISP filtering, or the target's firewall can all affect the result.

Is the check done from my computer?

No. The check is performed from our server, so your local firewall does not affect it — but it also cannot see ports blocked only on your network.
